Equivalence principle

Words: 32
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The equivalence principle states that gravity couples universally to energy-momentum and that a freely falling local frame removes uniform gravitational acceleration at a point. Tidal curvature remains measurable over a finite region.

Spacetime dimension

Words: 22
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The spacetime dimension is the dimension of the smooth manifold used to model spacetime. Ordinary general relativity uses one temporal and three spatial dimensions.

Killing vector field

Words: 222 Articles: 8
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A Killing vector field K generates a local one-parameter family of isometries. Equivalently,
LK​g=0⟺∇(μ​Kν)​=0.
(1)

Killing equation

Words: 75 Articles: 2
Killing vector field OurBigBook.com
Killing's equation is ∇(a​Kb)​=0. It says that the infinitesimal flow of K preserves the metric.

Second covariant derivative of a Killing vector

Words: 59 Articles: 1
Killing equation OurBigBook.com
For a Killing vector field and the curvature convention [∇μ​,∇ν​]Vα=Rαβμν​Vβ,
∇ν​∇μ​Kα=Rαμνβ​Kβ,∇μ​∇μKα=−Rαβ​Kβ.
(2)
The identity follows by combining the Ricci identity, Killing equation, and first Bianchi identity.
Killing vector preserves scalar curvature
Words: 36
Second covariant derivative of a Killing vector OurBigBook.com
Every Killing vector field K preserves the scalar curvature: LK​R=Kα∇α​R=0. One index proof rewrites this derivative as a doubly contracted curvature commutator acting on the antisymmetric tensor ∇[μ​Kλ]​; both terms vanish by symmetry of the Ricci tensor.

Geodesic conserved quantity from a Killing vector

Words: 23
Killing vector field OurBigBook.com
If U is the tangent to an affinely parametrized geodesic and K is a Killing vector, then g(K,U) is constant along the geodesic.

Stress-energy current from a Killing vector (Ja=Tab​Kb)

Words: 32
Killing vector field OurBigBook.com
If Tab is symmetric and covariantly conserved and K is a Killing vector field, then Ja=Tab​Kb is conserved. Its flux through a spacelike hypersurface is the energy or momentum charge generated by the isometry.

Komar charge

Words: 75 Articles: 2
Killing vector field OurBigBook.com
A Komar integral constructs a conserved gravitational charge from the exterior derivative of the one-form dual to a Killing vector. In four dimensions, a stationary mass is conventionally normalized as
MK​=−8π1​∫S​⋆dk.
(3)

Komar mass

Words: 18
Komar charge OurBigBook.com
Komar mass is the Komar charge associated with a stationary timelike Killing vector, using the normalization appropriate to gravitational mass.

Background-subtracted Komar energy

Words: 25
Komar charge OurBigBook.com
For a spacetime with a non-flat reference background, replacing k by k−kˉ removes the background contribution and can make the Komar surface integral finite.

Conformal Killing vector field

Words: 29 Articles: 1
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A conformal Killing vector field generates a local flow that preserves the metric up to a position-dependent scale factor.

Conformal Killing equation

Words: 10
Conformal Killing vector field OurBigBook.com
In d dimensions, the conformal Killing equation is
∇a​Xb​+∇b​Xa​=d2​gab​∇c​Xc.
(4)

Gravitational wave

Words: 315 Articles: 12
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A gravitational wave is a propagating disturbance of spacetime curvature produced by changing mass-energy multipole moments.

Gravitational-wave frequency (fGW​)

Words: 33
Gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
The gravitational-wave frequency is the temporal oscillation frequency of a radiative metric perturbation. A rigid source rotating with angular frequency ω and invariant under a half-turn radiates dominantly at angular frequency 2ω.

Quadrupole formula

Words: 22
Gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
For a slowly moving isolated source, the leading gravitational-wave luminosity is
P=5c5G​⟨Q...​​ij​Q...​​ij​⟩,
(5)
where Qij​ is the trace-free mass quadrupole moment.

Newman--Penrose formalism

Words: 75 Articles: 2
Gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
The Newman--Penrose formalism resolves spacetime curvature into scalars by contracting the Weyl tensor with a complex null tetrad.

Complex null tetrad

Words: 26
Newman--Penrose formalism OurBigBook.com
A complex null tetrad consists of two real null vectors and a complex-conjugate transverse pair, normalized so that the metric is reconstructed from their pairwise products.

Newman--Penrose scalar Psi4 (Ψ4​)

Words: 31
Newman--Penrose formalism OurBigBook.com
For a null tetrad (ℓ,k,m,mˉ), one common curvature-sign convention defines Ψ4​=Cμνρσ​kμmˉνkρmˉσ. In an outgoing wave zone it encodes the two transverse gravitational wave polarizations as one complex scalar.

Plane-fronted gravitational wave

Words: 169 Articles: 6
Gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
For
ds2=2dudv+dx2+dy2+H(u,x,y)du2,
(6)
the only potentially nonzero Ricci component is
Ruu​=−21​(Hxx​+Hyy​).
(7)
The vacuum equation is therefore the transverse Laplace equation.

Homogeneous wavefront of a plane gravitational wave

Words: 33
Plane-fronted gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
For a Brinkmann plane wave whose transverse profile is quadratic, Killing fields obtained from solutions of transverse oscillator equations act transitively on every constant-retarded-time wavefront. Each wavefront is therefore a homogeneous null hypersurface.

Rosen coordinates for a plane gravitational wave

Words: 24
Plane-fronted gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
Rosen coordinates put a plane wave into the transverse-metric form
ds2=−dudv+gAB​(u)dxAdxB.
(8)
For diagonal gAB​=diag(f2,g2), the only potentially nonzero Ricci tensor component is Ruu​=−f′′/f−g′′/g.

Gravitational-wave pulse

Words: 93 Articles: 3
Plane-fronted gravitational wave OurBigBook.com
A gravitational-wave pulse has curvature supported in a bounded interval of retarded time. Spacetime can be flat both before and after the pulse even though freely falling bodies retain a displacement or relative velocity produced while the pulse passed.
Gravitational-wave memory effect
Words: 55 Articles: 2
Gravitational-wave pulse OurBigBook.com
The gravitational-wave memory effect is a lasting change in the relative configuration of freely falling test bodies after a transient gravitational wave has passed.
Displacement memory
Words: 16
Gravitational-wave memory effect OurBigBook.com
Displacement memory is a persistent change in the separation of freely falling bodies after a gravitational-wave pulse.
Velocity memory
Words: 17
Gravitational-wave memory effect OurBigBook.com
Velocity memory is a persistent change in the relative velocity of freely falling bodies after a gravitational-wave pulse.

Covariant derivative

Words: 232 Articles: 8
General relativity OurBigBook.com
A connection defines covariant differentiation by adding one connection term for each contravariant index and subtracting one for each covariant index.

Covariant divergence

Words: 22
Covariant derivative OurBigBook.com
The covariant divergence contracts a covariant-derivative index with a contravariant tensor index. For a mixed rank-two tensor it is ∇μ​Tμν​.

Tensor type ((r,s))

Words: 113 Articles: 2
Covariant derivative OurBigBook.com
A tensor of type (r,s) has r contravariant and s covariant indices. Taking a covariant derivative adds one covariant index, while an outer tensor product adds the corresponding contravariant and covariant index counts.

Tensor component transformation law

Words: 43
Tensor type OurBigBook.com
Under a coordinate change x↦x′, the components of a type-(r,s) tensor acquire one forward Jacobian for each contravariant index and one inverse Jacobian for each covariant index. For a type-(1,1) tensor,
Tμ′ν′​=∂xα∂xμ′​∂xν′∂xβ​Tαβ​.
(9)

Identity tensor (idTM​=δμν​)

Words: 37
Tensor type OurBigBook.com
The identity tensor is the canonical type-(1,1) tensor that maps each tangent vector to itself. It pairs a covector η and vector V as η(V), and its components are the Kronecker delta δμν​ in every coordinate system.

Covariant derivative of a covariant tensor

Words: 9
Covariant derivative OurBigBook.com
For Wμν​,
∇α​Wμν​=∂α​Wμν​−Γαμρ​Wρν​−Γανρ​Wμρ​.
(10)

Levi-Civita connection

Words: 67 Articles: 2
Covariant derivative OurBigBook.com
The Levi-Civita connection is the unique torsion-free connection compatible with the metric; its coefficients are the Christoffel symbols formed from first metric derivatives.

Metric compatibility

Words: 17
Levi-Civita connection OurBigBook.com
Metric compatibility is ∇α​gμν​=0, allowing the metric to pass through covariant derivatives and index operations.

Lie derivative of an affine connection

Words: 27
Levi-Civita connection OurBigBook.com
The Lie derivative of a connection is the tensor
(LX​∇)Y​Z=LX​(∇Y​Z)−∇LX​Y​Z−∇Y​(LX​Z).
(11)
An isometry preserves the Levi-Civita connection, so LK​∇=0 for a Killing vector field.

Riemann curvature tensor

Words: 475 Articles: 21
General relativity OurBigBook.com
The Riemann tensor measures the failure of covariant derivatives to commute.

Curvature commutator on a covariant tensor

Words: 18
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
For a rank-two covariant tensor, the derivative commutator contributes one curvature action on each index:
[∇α​,∇β​]Wμν​=−Rρμαβ​Wρν​−Rρναβ​Wμρ​.
(12)

Curvature commutator on a contravariant tensor

Words: 15
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
For a type-(2,0) tensor, the Ricci identity acts once on each contravariant index:
[∇α​,∇β​]Tμν=Rμραβ​Tρν+Rνραβ​Tμρ.
(13)

Geodesic deviation

Words: 60 Articles: 1
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
For a family of affinely parametrized geodesics with tangent U and connecting field J, the Jacobi equation in the convention used here is
∇U​∇U​J=R(U,J)U.
(14)
It describes the relative acceleration produced by spacetime curvature.

Jacobi field

Words: 26
Geodesic deviation OurBigBook.com
A Jacobi field is the infinitesimal connecting vector between neighboring members of a one-parameter family of geodesics. It satisfies the geodesic-deviation equation along the reference geodesic.

Symmetric Hessian of a scalar field

Words: 10
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
For a torsion-free connection, Uμ​=∂μ​ϕ satisfies ∇α​Uβ​=∇β​Uα​.

First Bianchi identity

Words: 6
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
For a torsion-free connection, Rμαβγ​+Rμβγα​+Rμγαβ​=0.

Second Bianchi identity

Words: 18
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
For the Levi-Civita connection, the cyclic covariant derivative of curvature vanishes: ∇[e​Ra∣b∣cd]​=0. Contracting this identity gives the contracted Bianchi identity.

Weyl tensor (Cαβγδ​)

Words: 97 Articles: 2
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
The Weyl tensor is the completely trace-free part of the Riemann curvature tensor. In four dimensions,
Cαβγδ​=​Rαβγδ​−21​(gαγ​Rβδ​+gβδ​Rαγ​−gαδ​Rβγ​−gβγ​Rαδ​)+6R​(gαγ​gβδ​−gαδ​gβγ​).​
(15)

Trace-free property of the Weyl tensor

Words: 43
Weyl tensor OurBigBook.com
Every contraction of the Weyl tensor vanishes. Contracting its first and third indices directly cancels the Ricci and scalar-curvature terms; antisymmetry in each pair and symmetry under exchanging the two pairs reduce all other contractions to this one or make them vanish immediately.

Weyl tensor of a conformally flat metric

Words: 26
Weyl tensor OurBigBook.com
Every conformally flat metric in dimension at least four has identically zero Weyl tensor. The Weyl tensor is the obstruction to local conformal flatness in dimensions at least four.

First-pair antisymmetry of the Riemann tensor

Words: 11
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
Applying the curvature commutator to the parallel metric gives Rμαβγ​=−Rαμβγ​.

Ricci tensor

Words: 197 Articles: 8
Riemann curvature tensor OurBigBook.com
The Ricci tensor is the contraction Rαβ​=Rμαμβ​ and is symmetric for the Levi-Civita connection.

Ricci tensor in two dimensions

Under the null energy condition and the usual global assumptions excluding naked pathologies, the area of every cross-section of a future event horizon is nondecreasing toward the future. The Null Raychaudhuri equation and future completeness rule out negative expansion of its generators.
Hawking's area theorem
Words: 31
Second law of black-hole mechanics OurBigBook.com
Hawking's area theorem states that the total area of classical future event horizons cannot decrease when the null energy condition and the required global assumptions hold. It is the geometric content of the second law of black-hole mechanics.

Third law of black-hole mechanics

Words: 22
Black-hole thermodynamics OurBigBook.com
The third law of black-hole mechanics says that no finite physical process can reduce the surface gravity of a regular black-hole horizon to zero.

Generalized second law

Words: 22
Black-hole thermodynamics OurBigBook.com
The generalized second law states that the sum of Bekenstein-Hawking entropy and the entropy of matter and radiation outside black holes does not decrease.

The Kerr ergoregion is the region where the asymptotically timelike stationary Killing field becomes spacelike. Its outer boundary is r=M+M2−a2cos2θ​.
Penrose process
Words: 32
Kerr ergoregion OurBigBook.com
The Penrose process extracts rotational energy by allowing a fragment with negative stationary Killing energy to enter the black hole while another fragment escapes with more energy than the original body carried.

On the Kerr symmetry axis, the radial metric has F=Δ/(r2+a2) and the tortoise coordinate satisfies dr∗​/dr=F−1=(r2+a2)/Δ.

It is positive for 23​−3​<∣a∣/M<1, diverges at the lower endpoint, and tends to zero in the extremal limit.

Stationary spacetime

General relativity OurBigBook.com
A stationary spacetime admits a Killing vector field that is timelike in the region representing stationary observers, in particular near infinity for an asymptotically flat stationary black hole.

Strictly stationary spacetime

A strictly stationary spacetime has a globally defined Killing vector that is timelike everywhere.

Static spacetime

Words: 52 Articles: 1
Stationary spacetime OurBigBook.com
A static spacetime has a timelike Killing vector that is hypersurface orthogonal. Coordinates adapted to it can be chosen with no time-space cross terms.

Static spacetime OurBigBook.com
The stress-energy current from a Killing vector associated with the static time translation gives a positive conserved energy for a massive real scalar. Its hypersurface independence follows from current conservation and the divergence theorem.

Stationary axisymmetric spacetime

A stationary axisymmetric spacetime has commuting stationary and axial Killing vector fields, with the axial field having closed spacelike orbits.

The spatial covariant derivative projects the spacetime covariant derivative and every free tensor index onto a spatial hypersurface. It is the Levi-Civita connection of the induced spatial metric.

Geodesic slicing chooses unit lapse and zero shift, so the hypersurface normals are affinely parametrized timelike geodesics. It is simple but commonly develops coordinate singularities in finite time.

An asymptotically flat spacetime approaches Minkowski spacetime sufficiently far from isolated sources. At null infinity this is stated invariantly by requiring a smooth conformal completion whose boundary contains future and past null infinity.

A conformal completion embeds a physical spacetime (M,g) into a manifold with boundary carrying a regular metric gˉ​=Ω2g. Infinity is represented by Ω=0 with dΩ=0; the causal character of each boundary component is determined by gˉ​ab∇ˉa​Ω∇ˉb​Ω.

Words: 29

Future null infinity is the boundary reached by future-directed outgoing null geodesics in an asymptotically flat spacetime. In four dimensions it has topology R×S2 under the standard asymptotic-flatness assumptions.

Gravitational lensing is the deflection and focusing of light by spacetime curvature along the line of sight.

Gravitational microlensing is lensing by compact masses whose individual image splitting is unresolved, so their motion is observed through time-dependent magnification.
